title: Reconcile Stripe/NetSuite exports and fix proration edge-case billing deltas
creator: Aarav Patel
description:
Summary:
There are persistent mismatches between exported Stripe invoices (and invoice items) and the downstream NetSuite import. The largest diffs occur when subscriptions change mid-cycle (plan upgrades/downgrades) where Stripe creates prorated invoice items and our NetSuite mapping either drops lines or aggregates them incorrectly, causing invoice amount deltas and customer disputes.

Symptoms observed:
- NetSuite totals for March invoices were ~0.7% higher than Stripe exported totals for 120 customers; variance concentrated on prorated subscriptions.
- Reconciliation job flags group A (proration) as 'unmatched' because our export job only exports top-level invoice totals for subscription changes, not individual invoice_item entries with prorations and negative adjustments.
- Rounding behavior: Stripe sends amounts in cents, but our aggregator applied float rounding then re-converted leading to off-by-one-cent errors across many lines.
- Edge case: when rate-limit throttles usage-export worker, duplicate usage submissions have been collapsed incorrectly and subsequently cause net-new invoice items in Stripe not reflected in nightly export snapshot.

Impact:
- Customer billing disputes and support tickets (5 escalations last week).
- Revenue recognition mismatches for finance; manual adjustments required.

Goal:
Fix export/reconciliation pipeline to ensure one-to-one mapping between Stripe invoice items and NetSuite import rows, handle proration line items precisely, harden rounding to cents, and eliminate duplicate-usage collapse errors caused by rate-limited exporters. Ship migration/backfill for prior month mismatches and add monitoring to detect regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly Stripe export contains invoice_item_id-level lines for all invoices including prorations
NetSuite import mapping accepts invoice_item_id as primary key and preserves sign and cents exactly
Reconciliation job diff rate reduced to <0.05% for prorations over a 7-day baseline
Backfill job runs to correct March mismatches and creates audit log entries for manual finance review
Unit + integration tests for rounding and proration edge cases included in CI
Runbook updated; Slack alert channel & dashboard tile for proration diffs
work_log: 2026-02-16: Initial report from Finance showing March/Stripe vs NetSuite discrepancy (ticket FIN-184). Assigned to billing reliability squad.
2026-02-18: Repro steps saved: reproduce using subscription fixtures: plan-small -> upgrade mid-cycle to plan-medium (see ./fixtures/proration-upgrade.json in billing repo).

2026-02-22: Investigated Stripe export: found export job aggregated invoice-level totals for subscription updates rather than emitting invoice_items. Patch proposed to include invoice_item rows (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/312).
2026-02-25: Discovered rounding bug: intermediate float sum used in exporter. Switched to integer cents arithmetic in local branch. Added unit tests for fractional cent flows.

2026-02-28: Rate-limit related duplicate usage collapse: traced to usage-export worker where retry/backoff collapsed two near-identical usage events into one aggregate with wrong quantity. Filed ENG-4818 to harden usage dedupe logic.

2026-03-03: Sync with Finance & PM. Decided on two-phase rollout: 1) Export change + tests 2) NetSuite mapping update + backfill. Document link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/billing/recon-proration-plan
2026-03-05: NetSuite mapping patch prepared (internal import mapping sheet version v2). Spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/billing/netsuite-mapping-v2.xlsx
2026-03-07: PR review feedback from Lydia (Finance) requesting invoice_item_id present as the last column and original_stripe_amount_cents retained; updated PR accordingly.

2026-03-09: Deployed exporter patch to staging. Nightly reconciliation ran: proration diffs dropped from 0.7% to 0.12% for staging dataset. Observed two remaining classes of failures: legacy invoices with manual adjustments and very old subscriptions using legacy meter. Preparing backfill plan.

2026-03-10: Started writing backfill job to reconcile March mismatches. Backfill will: export historical invoice_item rows from Stripe API, compute expected NetSuite rows, and create CSV for Finance to import with audit metadata.
steps_to_reproduce: Create subscription S on plan A on 2026-02-01
Upgrade subscription S to plan B on 2026-02-16 via the customer portal (creates prorated invoice items in Stripe)
Run nightly exporter job (billing-exporter) to produce Stripe CSVs; observe if invoice_item_id rows are present
Import exported CSV into NetSuite staging import; verify sign and cents preservation
If mismatch occurs, inspect exporter log for rounding warnings and usage-export worker retry events
implementation_notes: Exporter: switch all amount math to integer cents and avoid float conversions. Add explicit invoice_item_id, subscription_id, invoice_id, and currency columns to the CSV export.

NetSuite mapping: adjust import template to use invoice_item_id as natural key. Preserve original Stripe amount and a 'proration_flag' when quantity != 1 or when invoice_item.description contains 'proration'.
Reconciliation: add matching by invoice_item_id then fallback to (invoice_id + description + amount_cents) with strict tie-breaker rules.
Backfill: use Stripe API pagination to collect historical invoice_item list for the afflicted date range (2026-02-01 -> 2026-03-31). Produce an audit CSV with reconciliation_reason column.
Monitoring: add Grafana panel to show percent of invoices with unmatched prorations, alert at 0.2% for 6h sustained.

Rate limiting: adjust usage-export worker to persist interim events to S3 before dedupe so transient rate-limit retries don't collapse distinct events. Add idempotency key generation per usage_event_id + sequence.
Tests: create integration harness that spins up a local Stripe-mock and NetSuite-import-simulator for CI smoke tests; include edge-case fixtures (negative prorations, cents rounding).
